Economists divide the population of a country into several groups. People who have a job are called the employed. They may work full-time or part-time, for a company or for themselves. A person who runs his or her own business is self-employed.

People who do not have a job but are actively looking for one are called the unemployed. It is important to understand that not everyone without a job is unemployed. Students, pensioners and people who look after their children at home and do not look for work are not part of the labour force at all.

The labour force, or workforce, includes both the employed and the unemployed. The unemployment rate shows what percentage of the labour force has no job. For example, if a country has 100 million people in the labour force and 4 million of them are looking for work, the unemployment rate is 4%.

There is also a group that statistics often miss: the underemployed. These are people who work part-time but want a full-time job, or people whose job does not use their qualifications. A graduate in economics who works as a courier is a typical example.

Unemployment is never zero, even in a strong economy. Economists usually describe three main types of unemployment, and each of them has different causes.

Frictional unemployment is short-term. It appears when people leave one job and spend some time looking for a better one, or when young people finish university and search for their first job. This type of unemployment is natural: it takes time to find the right job, and employers need time to choose the right candidate.

Structural unemployment is more serious. It happens when the structure of the economy changes and workers' skills no longer match the jobs that are available. For example, when factories install robots, some workers lose their jobs and cannot find similar work. They often need vocational training or retraining to change their profession.

Cyclical unemployment depends on the business cycle. During a recession, demand for goods and services falls, companies produce less and lay off staff. When the economy grows again, companies start hiring and cyclical unemployment goes down.

Governments fight each type in a different way: job websites and job centres reduce frictional unemployment, retraining programmes help with structural unemployment, and economic policy is used against cyclical unemployment.

Finding the right person for a job is one of the main tasks of an HR department. The process is called recruitment, and it usually starts when a vacancy appears: an employee resigns, retires or is promoted, or the company grows and needs new staff.

First, the HR manager writes a job description, which lists the duties and responsibilities of the position, and a person specification, which describes the qualifications, skills and experience the ideal candidate should have. Then the company advertises the vacancy on job websites, on social networks or through a recruitment agency. For senior positions, companies sometimes use headhunters.

Applicants send their CVs and cover letters or fill in an application form. The HR department reads all applications and makes a shortlist of the best candidates. These candidates are invited for an interview. Some companies also use tests to check the candidates' skills.

After the interviews, the company checks the references of the best candidate and makes a job offer. If the candidate accepts it, he or she signs an employment contract. The new employee usually has a probation period of up to three months, and onboarding helps him or her to get used to the new workplace.

When a person gets a job, the employer and the employee sign an employment contract. This document protects both sides: it says what the employee must do and what the employer must give in return. In Russia, the rules for employment contracts are set by the Labour Code.

A typical contract includes the job title and duties, the place of work, working hours, the amount of salary and when it is paid, the length of annual leave and the benefits the employee will receive. It may also say if there is a probation period.

Contracts can be permanent or fixed-term. A permanent contract has no end date, so it gives the worker more job security. A fixed-term contract ends on a particular date; it is often used for seasonal or temporary work, or to replace an employee who is on maternity leave.

If the employee works more hours than the contract says, this is overtime, and by law it must be paid at a higher rate. Either side can end the contract, but they must follow the rules: an employee who wants to resign usually has to give two weeks' notice, and an employer cannot dismiss a worker without a legal reason.

People leave their jobs for many different reasons, and English has different words for each situation. If you decide to leave because you have found a better job or you are not happy, you resign or quit. Usually you write a resignation letter and hand in your notice.
When people stop working because of their age, they retire and start receiving a pension. In Russia the retirement age is gradually rising.

Sometimes the decision is made by the employer. If a worker is dismissed because of bad work or bad behaviour, for example, regular absenteeism, we say that he was fired or got the sack. These are informal expressions; in official documents the word dismissal is used.

Redundancy is different. A worker is made redundant when the company no longer needs his job, for example, because a department closes or the company is losing money. It is not the worker's fault, so he usually receives severance pay. In American English, the phrase lay off is often used for this situation.
A person who has lost a job can register at a job centre, receive unemployment benefit and get help with job hunting.

Labour, like any other product, has a price. The price of labour is the money that workers receive for their work. In English, there are two main words for it. A salary is a fixed amount of money paid every month, usually to office workers and specialists. A wage is usually paid per hour or per week, often to manual workers.

The level of pay depends on supply and demand on the labour market. If there is a labour shortage in a profession, for example, in IT or medicine, employers have to offer higher salaries. If many people can do a job, the pay is usually lower.

The state also influences wages. In most countries, including Russia, the law sets a minimum wage, the lowest amount an employer can pay. Trade unions negotiate with employers and sign collective agreements to protect workers' pay.

Money is not the only reward. Many companies offer benefits, such as health insurance, a company car or free meals, and incentives, such as bonuses and commission, to motivate staff. Together, salary and benefits are called the remuneration package. HR managers know that a good package helps to attract talented people and reduce staff turnover.

Human resource management, or HRM, is the management of people in an organisation. People are the most valuable resource of any company, because machines and money cannot work without them.

The main aim of HRM is to help the company reach its goals by attracting, developing and keeping the right employees. HR managers deal with many tasks: workforce planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, performance appraisal, pay and benefits, and employee relations.

In the past, this area was called personnel management, and it was mostly about paperwork: contracts, holidays and wages. Today HRM is more strategic. HR managers take part in business decisions and help to build a strong corporate culture.

In my opinion, HRM is especially important now, because there is a labour shortage in many industries, and companies have to compete for talented people. That is why I chose this profession, and I hope to become a good HR specialist in the future.

An HR manager is a specialist who is responsible for the people in a company. He or she reports to the general director and works closely with the heads of all departments.

The duties of an HR manager are very different. He or she writes job descriptions, places job advertisements, interviews candidates, prepares employment contracts and organises onboarding for new staff. The HR manager also plans training, deals with conflicts, keeps personnel records and makes sure that the company follows labour law.

To be successful, an HR manager needs special personal qualities. First of all, good communication skills, because the job is about people. Second, he or she must be fair, patient and able to keep information confidential. Finally, a modern HR manager should understand economics, psychology and law.
I think it is a difficult but interesting job. You never do the same thing twice, and you can really change people’s lives when you help them find a good job.

Recruitment is the process of finding and attracting candidates for a vacancy. Selection is the process of choosing the best candidate from all applicants.

Recruitment can be internal or external. Internal recruitment means that a vacancy is filled by a person who already works in the company, for example, through promotion. It is cheaper and motivates staff. External recruitment means looking for people outside the company: through job websites, social networks, recruitment agencies or headhunters. It brings new ideas, but it takes more time and money.

The selection process usually includes several stages: screening CVs and making a shortlist, interviews, tests, and checking references. After that the company makes a job offer to the best candidate.
Mistakes in recruitment are very expensive. If the company hires the wrong person, it loses money on training, and staff turnover grows. That is why HR managers must plan every stage carefully.

A job interview is a formal meeting where an employer asks a candidate questions to find out if he or she is suitable for the job. It is one of the most important stages of selection.

Interviews can be face-to-face, by phone or online. There can be one interviewer or a panel of several people. Typical questions are: Tell me about yourself; Why do you want to work for our company; What are your strengths and weaknesses; Where do you see yourself in five years.

To succeed at an interview, a candidate should prepare well. He or she should find information about the company, think about answers to typical questions, dress smartly and arrive on time. During the interview it is important to be polite, confident and honest, and at the end to ask a couple of questions about the job.
Personally, I think the most difficult question is about weaknesses. The best answer is to name a real weakness and explain how you are working on it.

When people apply for a job, they usually send a CV and a cover letter. CV stands for curriculum vitae, which means “the course of life” in Latin.

A good CV is short, usually one or two pages. It includes personal details and contact information, a short profile, work experience starting with the most recent job, education, skills such as languages and computer programs, and sometimes hobbies. Many employers also ask for references.

A cover letter is a short letter that you send together with your CV. In it, you say which position you are applying for, explain why you are interested in the job and why you are a good candidate. The letter should be polite, formal and without mistakes.

An HR manager often has only half a minute to look at one CV, so it must be clear and easy to read. I think the most common mistakes are spelling mistakes, too much text and information that has nothing to do with the job.

An employment contract is an agreement between an employer and an employee. In Russia it must be in writing, and its rules are set by the Labour Code.
The contract states the job title and duties, the place of work, working hours, salary, annual leave and benefits. It can also include a probation period, which usually lasts up to three months.

There are two main types of contracts. A permanent contract has no end date and gives the employee job security. A fixed-term contract ends on a certain date; it is used for temporary or seasonal work.

Working conditions are also very important. They include the working schedule, for example full-time, part-time, shift work or flexitime, the safety of the workplace and the possibility to work remotely. Nowadays many young people prefer flexible working hours and remote work, so modern companies try to offer them.

Part-time employment means working fewer hours, for example, twenty hours a week. It is popular among students and parents with small children. Temporary employment is work for a limited period, for example, seasonal work in summer.

Unemployment is a situation when people who are able and want to work cannot find a job. The unemployment rate shows the percentage of the labour force without work.

The government fights unemployment in different ways. Job centres help people find work, retraining programmes teach new professions, and the state supports small business. Nowadays the unemployment rate in Russia is quite low, and many companies have the opposite problem: a labour shortage.

Motivation is what makes people want to work well. Motivated employees are more productive, make fewer mistakes and stay in the company longer.

There are two kinds of motivation. Financial incentives include salary, bonuses, commission and benefits such as health insurance. Non-financial motivation includes interesting work, praise, training, career prospects, a good team and a comfortable workplace.

Job satisfaction is the feeling of being happy with your job. It depends not only on money but also on relationships with colleagues and the supervisor, workload and the balance between work and private life. Low job satisfaction leads to absenteeism and high staff turnover.

I believe that money is important, but it is not everything. For example, many young people choose a company because it offers training, flexible hours and a friendly atmosphere. The task of an HR manager is to find the right mix of incentives for every employee.

Pay is the money that employees receive for their work. It is often called the price of labour.

There are two main forms of pay. A salary is a fixed amount paid monthly, usually to office workers and specialists. A wage is paid per hour or per week, usually to manual workers. Some employees, for example salespeople, also get commission, a percentage of what they sell.

The level of pay depends on many factors: qualifications and experience, the industry, the region and the situation on the labour market. The state sets a minimum wage, and trade unions protect workers’ pay through collective agreements.

Besides money, many companies offer a benefits package: health insurance, paid meals, a company car, sports or training. Together with the salary, it is called the remuneration package. In my opinion, a good package is one of the main reasons why people choose an employer.

Employee relations are the relations between the employer and the employees. Good relations help the company work well and avoid conflicts.
A trade union is an organisation of workers that protects their rights and interests. Unions negotiate with employers about pay, working hours and safety, and sign collective agreements.
If the negotiations fail, workers can go on strike — they stop working as a protest. Strikes are expensive for both sides, so it is better to find a compromise.

The rights of workers are also protected by labour law. It forbids discrimination by age, sex or nationality and guarantees equal opportunities. An HR manager plays an important role here: he or she must listen to employees, solve conflicts and make sure that the company follows the law.

What is the role of the HR manager in employee relations?
To listen to employees, solve conflicts and follow the law.
The labour market is the place where employers look for workers and people look for jobs. The price of labour on this market is pay.

Today the Russian labour market has several features. First, the unemployment rate is very low. Second, there is a labour shortage in many areas: IT, engineering, medicine, construction and transport. That is why salaries in these areas grow fast.

Third, the market is changing because of new technologies. Some jobs disappear, and new professions appear, so people need lifelong learning. Remote work and freelancing are also becoming more popular, especially among young people.

For HR managers this situation is a challenge. They have to compete for good employees, offer attractive conditions and keep people in the company. I think that is why the HR profession is in high demand now.

The text is about how economists divide the population by employment status. First, it explains who the employed and the self-employed are. Then it says that the unemployed are people without a job who are looking for one, and that students and pensioners who don’t look for work are not in the labour force. The text also explains how the unemployment rate is calculated. Finally, it describes the underemployed — people who work part-time or below their qualifications.

The text deals with three types of unemployment. Frictional unemployment is short-term and happens when people are between jobs. Structural unemployment appears when workers’ skills no longer match the jobs, for example because of robots. Cyclical unemployment grows during a recession. The author concludes that governments fight each type in a different way.

The text describes the stages of recruitment. A vacancy appears, the HR manager writes a job description and a person specification and advertises the job. Then applicants send CVs, the company makes a shortlist and interviews the best candidates. Finally, it checks references, makes a job offer, and the new employee signs a contract and starts the probation period.

The text is about the employment contract. It explains that the contract protects both sides and lists what it usually includes. Then it compares permanent and fixed-term contracts. Finally, it says that overtime must be paid at a higher rate and that both sides must follow the rules when they end a contract.

The text explains different ways of leaving a job. People resign or quit when they decide to leave, and retire because of their age. They are fired when they work or behave badly, and made redundant when the company no longer needs their job. The text also says that redundant workers get severance pay and that people who lose a job can get help at a job centre.

The text deals with the price of labour. It explains the difference between a salary and a wage and says that pay depends on supply and demand on the labour market. Then it describes how the state and trade unions influence pay. Finally, it says that benefits and incentives are also part of the remuneration package, which helps to attract and keep good staff.
